knowledge_point.title: Expressing Flux Through a Surface as a Double Integral

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vector field $\mathbf F$ and the surface $S$ parametrized by $\mathbf r(u,v)$ for $D=(0,1)\times(0,1)$, where

$$
\mathbf F(x,y,z)=\left\langle 2 x z,\,- 3 y,\,3\right\rangle.
$$

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=\left\langle u v,\,u + v,\,1 - v\right\rangle.
$$

Orient $S$ in the direction of $\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v$.

If

$$
\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S=\iint_D (a u v^{2} + b v^{2} + c u v - 3 u + 3 v)\,\mathrm dA,
$$

what is the value of $a+b+c$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
The vector area element must agree with the specified orientation. First compute the tangent vectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u & =\left\langle v,\,1,\,0\right\rangle \\ \mathbf r_v & =\left\langle u,\,1,\,-1\right\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Their ordered cross product is

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v & =\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i&\mathbf j&\mathbf k\\v&1&0\\u&1&-1\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left\langle -1,\,v,\,- u + v\right\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Use $\mathbf N=\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v$.

For this orientation,

$$
\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S=\iint_D\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))\cdot\mathbf N(u,v)\,\mathrm dA.
$$

Substitute $x=u v$, $y=u + v$, $z=1 - v$ into the field:

$$
\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))=\left\langle - 2 u v^{2} + 2 u v,\,- 3 u - 3 v,\,3\right\rangle.
$$

Compute the three component contributions:

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{x} & =\left(- 2 u v^{2} + 2 u v\right)\left(-1\right) \\  & =2 u v^{2} - 2 u v \\ T_{y} & =\left(- 3 u - 3 v\right)\left(v\right) \\  & =- 3 u v - 3 v^{2} \\ T_{z} & =\left(3\right)\left(- u + v\right) \\  & =- 3 u + 3 v\end{aligned}
$$

Take the dot product component by component:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf F(\mathbf r)\cdot\mathbf N & =T_x+T_y+T_z \\  & =2 u v^{2} - 5 u v - 3 u - 3 v^{2} + 3 v\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S=\iint_D\left(2 u v^{2} - 5 u v - 3 u - 3 v^{2} + 3 v\right)\,\mathrm dA.
$$

Matching coefficients gives $a=2$, $b=-3$, $c=-5$. Hence

$$
a+b+c=(2)+(-3)+(-5)=-6.
$$

knowledge_point.title: Expressing Flux Through a Surface as a Double Integral

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vector field $\mathbf F$ and the surface $S$ parametrized by $\mathbf r(u,v)$ for $D=(0,1)\times(0,1)$, where

$$
\mathbf F(x,y,z)=\left\langle 3 z,\,2 x z,\,3 y z\right\rangle.
$$

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=\left\langle u,\,u^{2},\,v\right\rangle.
$$

Orient $S$ in the direction of $\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v$.

If

$$
\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S=\iint_D (a u v + b u^{2} v)\,\mathrm dA,
$$

what is the value of $a+b$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
The vector area element must agree with the specified orientation. First compute the tangent vectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u & =\left\langle 1,\,2 u,\,0\right\rangle \\ \mathbf r_v & =\left\langle 0,\,0,\,1\right\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Their ordered cross product is

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v & =\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i&\mathbf j&\mathbf k\\1&2 u&0\\0&0&1\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left\langle 2 u,\,-1,\,0\right\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Use $\mathbf N=\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v$.

For this orientation,

$$
\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S=\iint_D\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))\cdot\mathbf N(u,v)\,\mathrm dA.
$$

Substitute $x=u$, $y=u^{2}$, $z=v$ into the field:

$$
\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))=\left\langle 3 v,\,2 u v,\,3 u^{2} v\right\rangle.
$$

Compute the three component contributions:

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{x} & =\left(3 v\right)\left(2 u\right) \\  & =6 u v \\ T_{y} & =\left(2 u v\right)\left(-1\right) \\  & =- 2 u v \\ T_{z} & =\left(3 u^{2} v\right)\left(0\right) \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Take the dot product component by component:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf F(\mathbf r)\cdot\mathbf N & =T_x+T_y+T_z \\  & =4 u v\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S=\iint_D\left(4 u v\right)\,\mathrm dA.
$$

Matching coefficients gives $a=4$, $b=0$. Hence

$$
a+b=(4)+(0)=4.
$$

knowledge_point.title: Expressing Flux Through a Surface as a Double Integral

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vector field $\mathbf F$ and the surface $S$ parametrized by $\mathbf r(u,v)$ for $D=(0,1)\times(0,1)$, where

$$
\mathbf F(x,y,z)=\left\langle x^{2},\,- 2 x y,\,- 3 z\right\rangle.
$$

$$
\mathbf r(u,v)=\left\langle u,\,v,\,2 u v\right\rangle.
$$

Orient $S$ in the direction of $\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v$.

If

$$
\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S=\iint_D (a u v + b u^{2} v)\,\mathrm dA,
$$

what is the value of $a+b$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
The vector area element must agree with the specified orientation. First compute the tangent vectors:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u & =\left\langle 1,\,0,\,2 v\right\rangle \\ \mathbf r_v & =\left\langle 0,\,1,\,2 u\right\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Their ordered cross product is

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v & =\begin{vmatrix}\mathbf i&\mathbf j&\mathbf k\\1&0&2 v\\0&1&2 u\end{vmatrix} \\  & =\left\langle - 2 v,\,- 2 u,\,1\right\rangle\end{aligned}
$$

Use $\mathbf N=\mathbf r_u\times\mathbf r_v$.

For this orientation,

$$
\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S=\iint_D\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))\cdot\mathbf N(u,v)\,\mathrm dA.
$$

Substitute $x=u$, $y=v$, $z=2 u v$ into the field:

$$
\mathbf F(\mathbf r(u,v))=\left\langle u^{2},\,- 2 u v,\,- 6 u v\right\rangle.
$$

Compute the three component contributions:

$$
\begin{aligned}T_{x} & =\left(u^{2}\right)\left(- 2 v\right) \\  & =- 2 u^{2} v \\ T_{y} & =\left(- 2 u v\right)\left(- 2 u\right) \\  & =4 u^{2} v \\ T_{z} & =\left(- 6 u v\right)\left(1\right) \\  & =- 6 u v\end{aligned}
$$

Take the dot product component by component:

$$
\begin{aligned}\mathbf F(\mathbf r)\cdot\mathbf N & =T_x+T_y+T_z \\  & =2 u^{2} v - 6 u v\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\iint_S\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf S=\iint_D\left(2 u^{2} v - 6 u v\right)\,\mathrm dA.
$$

Matching coefficients gives $a=-6$, $b=2$. Hence

$$
a+b=(-6)+(2)=-4.
$$
